outcome: mode of delivery preference (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
cohort: Pregnant women (18+ years, singleton pregnancy between 20-40 gestational weeks, no high-risk conditions) attending an obstetrics and gynecology clinic in Turkey.
finding: A higher perception of traumatic birth was significantly associated with a decreased preference for vaginal delivery and an increased likelihood of choosing cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: 71.8% of participants preferred cesarean section over vaginal delivery, and a higher perception of traumatic birth was linked to a decreased preference for vaginal delivery.
